symptoms: Yellowing or pale leaves reported by farmer
possible_causes: Nutrient availability, water stress, natural leaf ageing, pest damage, or disease are possibilities; this report alone cannot distinguish them.
investigate: Record whether older or younger leaves are affected
Photograph the affected plant and a healthy comparison plant
Check whether symptoms are spreading
Review soil moisture, irrigation, drainage, and any recent inputs
immediate_actions: Mark affected plants and repeat observations in 3–7 days
Avoid applying fertilizer or pesticide until the cause and local guidance are checked
avoid: Do not diagnose a nutrient deficiency from leaf colour alone
Do not apply pesticide or fertilizer solely from this alert
leaf_yellowing.expert_help: Contact a local agricultural extension officer if symptoms spread, many plants are affected, or disease is suspected.

source.title: Symptom report is a scouting prompt; diagnosis requires field assessment

wilting.problem: Reported wilting or possible water stress
possible_causes: Low available soil moisture, interrupted irrigation, root damage, waterlogging, heat, or disease are possibilities.
investigate: Check soil moisture in the root zone
Inspect irrigation delivery and recent rainfall
Look for standing water or damaged roots
Record whether wilting persists in cooler hours
immediate_actions: Verify soil and irrigation conditions before changing water application
Record a follow-up observation within 1–3 days
avoid: Do not increase irrigation without checking for standing water and drainage
Do not infer a disease from wilting alone
wilting.expert_help: Seek local extension advice if wilting persists after soil and irrigation checks or appears with stem/root symptoms.

waterlogging.problem: Reported standing water or possible waterlogging
symptoms: Standing water or poor drainage reported by farmer
possible_causes: Blocked drainage, over-irrigation, local topography, or heavy rainfall are possibilities.
investigate: Record where and how long water remains
Inspect field outlets and nearby low areas
Check soil texture and recent rainfall/irrigation
Photograph affected and unaffected areas
immediate_actions: Inspect drainage and irrigation delivery; consult local guidance before altering field channels
avoid: Do not prescribe a drainage redesign without field topography and soil assessment
waterlogging.expert_help: Seek local extension or irrigation advice if water remains or crop symptoms worsen.

possible_causes: Insect feeding or other physical damage are possibilities; pest identity is unconfirmed.
investigate: Record affected plant parts and the number of plants affected
Photograph the symptom and any insect or frass without disturbing it
Check whether damage is spreading and record the date
immediate_actions: Continue scouting and preserve a clear photo/sample for local diagnosis
Use a locally validated integrated-pest-management recommendation after identification
avoid: Do not apply pesticide before identifying the pest and checking current local registration and label directions
suspected_pest.expert_help: Contact a local agricultural extension officer or plant-protection specialist for identification and current control advice.

possible_causes: Disease, nutrient or water stress, and physical injury can produce overlapping symptoms; diagnosis is unconfirmed.
investigate: Photograph affected leaves, stalks, and a healthy comparison
Record the plant part, symptom pattern, spread, and recent weather
Note whether symptoms are clustered or scattered
immediate_actions: Avoid moving planting material from affected plants until the symptom is assessed
Arrange expert identification when symptoms spread
avoid: Do not diagnose or prescribe chemical treatment from one symptom or photograph
suspected_disease.expert_help: Seek local extension or plant pathology advice, especially if stalk symptoms or rapid spread are present.

tiller_decline.problem: Tiller count decreased between comparable observations
symptoms: A recorded tiller count is lower than the previous count for the same cycle and sample area.
possible_causes: Sampling variation, crop damage, competition, moisture conditions, or natural tiller survival are possibilities.
investigate: Confirm the same area, row length, and counting method were used
Repeat the count in a nearby marked area
Inspect for crop damage, weeds, soil moisture, and drainage
immediate_actions: Verify the count before changing inputs
Record the repeat count and field conditions
avoid: Do not apply additional fertilizer automatically from a single declining count
tiller_decline.expert_help: Seek local advice if a verified decline continues or accompanies visible crop stress.

height_decline.problem: Recorded plant height decreased between observations
symptoms: A height measurement is lower than the previous measurement.
possible_causes: Different sampled plants, measurement method, lodging, breakage, or data-entry error are possibilities.
investigate: Check that the same height definition and unit were used
Repeat measurements on representative plants
Inspect for lodging, breakage, and visible damage
immediate_actions: Correct the record if it was a measurement or entry error; otherwise document the affected plants
avoid: Do not interpret a lower sample mean as proof of disease or poor growth
height_decline.expert_help: Seek local advice if repeated measurements confirm damage or abnormal symptoms.
